questions.explanation: „Das Klima“ plus „der Wandel“, change, gives climate change. The weather forecast is „der Wetterbericht“ and air conditioning „die Klimaanlage“.
„Der Schutz“ is protection, as in „Datenschutz“ and „Sonnenschutz“. Pollution is „die Umweltverschmutzung“, which shares the first half.
„Nachhaltig“ means sustainable, living in a way that can last without using up resources. „Nach“ looks like 'after', but „nachher“ is the word for 'afterwards'.
„Erneuern“ is to renew, so these are sources such as wind, sun and water. Coal, oil and gas are „fossile Brennstoffe“, the opposite.

questions.stem: What does „die Energiewende“ refer to in Germany?
options: The shift from fossil and nuclear power to renewable energy
A sudden rise in the price of electricity during the winter months
The change between summer time and winter time
A turbine that turns wind into electricity
questions.explanation: „Die Wende“ is a turning point, and the „Energiewende“ is the long-term move to renewable sources. A wind turbine is „die Windkraftanlage“ or „das Windrad“.

options: Dumping household rubbish illegally in the forest at night
Sorting rubbish into separate bins for recycling
questions.explanation: „Trennen“ is to separate, so households sort paper, glass, packaging and organic waste. Collection is „die Müllabfuhr“.

options: A nature trail through the forest
A footprint left by a wild animal
questions.explanation: It measures how much of the earth's resources one person's way of life uses. The phrase is a direct match for the English term, which makes it easier than most.
„Verschwenden“ is to waste, and „Lebensmittel“ are foodstuffs. A shortage would be „der Mangel“, and poisoning „die Lebensmittelvergiftung“.

questions.stem: Read: „Seit unsere Stadt das Zentrum autofrei gemacht hat, fahren viel mehr Leute mit dem Rad. Die Geschäftsleute hatten Angst, Kunden zu verlieren – das Gegenteil ist passiert.“ What happened to the shops?
options: They lost customers, as they had feared
They moved out of the town centre
They closed while the work was done
They gained customers, despite their fears
questions.explanation: „Das Gegenteil“ is 'the opposite', so the feared loss of customers turned into a gain. A reader who stops at „Angst, Kunden zu verlieren“ chooses the reverse.

questions.stem: Read: „Einerseits ist Windkraft sauber, andererseits stören sich manche Anwohner an dem Lärm der Anlagen.“ What objection is mentioned?
options: Wind power is not clean enough
The turbines are far too expensive for towns to build
Wind power is unreliable in summer
The noise bothers some people who live nearby
questions.explanation: „Einerseits … andererseits“ weighs one side against the other. „Anwohner“ are residents, „der Lärm“ is noise, and cleanliness is the point in favour.

questions.stem: What does „die Vielfalt“ mean, as in „kulturelle Vielfalt“?
questions.explanation: „Viel“ is 'many', and „die Vielfalt“ is variety or diversity. The majority is „die Mehrheit“.

questions.stem: What does „ein Mensch mit Migrationshintergrund“ mean?
options: A person who, or whose parents, migrated to the country
A person who is about to leave the country for good next year
A person who works in an office that helps migrants
A person who studies the history of migration
questions.explanation: The term covers people who migrated themselves and those with at least one parent who did. It describes background, not plans to move, which is what „auswandern“ would express.

questions.stem: Why is „die Heimat“ hard to translate into English?
options: It is a formal legal term used only in official documents
It is a dialect word used only in northern Germany
It means the place where you feel you belong, not just a country
It means a building and nothing more, so 'home' says far too much
questions.explanation: „Heimat“ joins place, childhood and belonging, so 'homeland' or 'home' each catch only part of it. It is one of the terms the study design means by 'no direct equivalent'.
„Das Weh“ is pain, so „Heimweh“ is the ache for home. Housework is „die Hausarbeit“.

options: A longing to travel far away
A pain that comes from a distance
questions.explanation: „Fern“ is far, and „Fernweh“ is the opposite of „Heimweh“: an ache for distant places. Television is „das Fernsehen“, which shares only the first part.
„Der Bürger“ is a citizen, so a „Weltbürger“ sees themselves as part of the whole world. A world champion is „ein Weltmeister“.
„Mehr“ is more and „die Sprache“ language, so „Mehrsprachigkeit“ is speaking several languages. Translation is „die Übersetzung“, and sign language „die Gebärdensprache“.
„Gleich“ is equal and „das Recht“ a right, so it is equality of rights, for example between men and women. Equal pay is narrower: „gleiche Bezahlung“ or „Lohngleichheit“.

questions.stem: Read: „Immer mehr Touristen besuchen unser kleines Dorf am See. Für die Einwohner bedeutet das Einnahmen, aber auch volle Straßen und hohe Mieten.“ What does tourism bring the residents?
options: Crowded streets, but lower rents for locals
New jobs, but no extra income for the village
Income, but also crowded streets and high rents
Income, and quieter streets than before
questions.explanation: „Einnahmen“ are earnings, and „aber auch“ adds the costs: „volle Straßen“ and „hohe Mieten“. Each wrong answer reverses one of the three points.

questions.stem: What does „die Unterkunft“ mean when planning a trip?
questions.explanation: „Eine Unterkunft suchen“ is to look for somewhere to stay. Arrival is „die Ankunft“, which looks very similar.

options: Tourism designed for elderly or slow-moving travellers
Relaxing holidays at a health spa
Tourism that respects nature and local people
questions.explanation: „Sanft“ is gentle, and „sanfter Tourismus“ is the alternative to „Massentourismus“, mass tourism: small-scale, low-impact travel that benefits the region. It has nothing to do with the age or pace of the traveller.

questions.stem: Read the station announcement: „Wegen Bauarbeiten fällt der Zug nach Salzburg heute aus. Bitte nutzen Sie den Schienenersatzverkehr. Die Busse fahren vor dem Haupteingang ab.“ What should passengers for Salzburg do?
options: Wait on the platform for a later train to Salzburg
Take the train from another platform after the building work
Buy a new ticket at the main entrance for a bus
Take a replacement bus from outside the main entrance
questions.explanation: „Fällt aus“ means the train is cancelled, and „Schienenersatzverkehr“ is the replacement service for a rail line, here by bus. „Vor dem Haupteingang“ is 'in front of the main entrance'.
„Die Werbung“ is advertising, and „werben für“ is to advertise. Applying for a job is „die Bewerbung“, one prefix away.
„Der Bildschirm“ is a screen, literally 'picture shield'. „Die Bildung“ is education, a different word.
„Das Mobbing“ is bullying in German, a borrowed word with a new meaning, and „Cyber-“ puts it online. Hacking is „das Hacken“.
„Die Daten“ are data, and „der Schutz“ is protection, so it covers privacy rules on personal information. Storage is „die Speicherung“.
„Die Privatsphäre“ is the private sphere, a person's privacy, often in the phrase „die Privatsphäre schützen“. Private property is „das Privateigentum“.

options: An incorrect answer in a test
questions.explanation: „Die Meldung“ is a news item or report, so a „Falschmeldung“ is a report that is untrue. A mistake in general is „der Fehler“.

questions.stem: What does „laut“ mean in „Laut einer Studie schlafen Jugendliche zu wenig“?
questions.explanation: As a preposition, „laut“ means 'according to' and introduces a source. As an adjective it means loud, which makes no sense here.

questions.stem: Read: „Viele Jugendliche informieren sich hauptsächlich über soziale Medien. Experten warnen jedoch, dass dort nicht jede Nachricht stimmt.“ What do the experts warn?
options: Every news item online is false
Not every news item on social media is true
Young people do not read the news
Social media is used only by experts and journalists
questions.explanation: „Nicht jede Nachricht stimmt“ is 'not every item is correct', which is weaker than saying all are false. „Jedoch“ signals the contrast with the first sentence.

questions.stem: Read the advertisement: „Jetzt zugreifen! Nur noch heute: zwei Paar Schuhe zum Preis von einem!“ Which technique does it use?
options: An appeal to environmental values and nature
questions.explanation: „Nur noch heute“ is 'today only', and the imperative „Jetzt zugreifen!“, 'grab it now', pushes the reader to act at once. No person, science or environmental claim is mentioned.

questions.stem: Which word in an article signals that the writer is about to introduce a contrasting point?
questions.explanation: „Jedoch“ means 'however'. „Außerdem“ adds a point, „deshalb“ draws a consequence and „zum Beispiel“ gives an example, so only „jedoch“ turns the argument.
„Forschen“ is to research, and „der Forscher“ is a researcher. Progress is „der Fortschritt“, a word often used alongside it.
„Erfinden“ is to invent; to discover is „entdecken“, so a discovery is „die Entdeckung“. The two are close in meaning but not the same.
„KI“ is artificial intelligence, „künstlich“ meaning artificial. The English abbreviation AI is also understood in German.

options: The spread of digital technology through society and work
The repair of broken laptops, computers and other digital devices
The counting of numbers with the fingers
The banning of mobile phones in schools
questions.explanation: „Die Digitalisierung“ is the move of work, school and services onto digital systems. It is a common topic in debates about the future of work.

questions.stem: What does „Homeoffice“ mean to a German speaker?
options: A study room in a house
questions.explanation: „Im Homeoffice arbeiten“ is to work from home. It looks English, but in British English the Home Office is a government department, so the borrowing has its own German meaning.
„Eine große Herausforderung“ is a big challenge. „Herausfordern“ is to challenge; a demand for payment is „die Forderung“.

options: To save up for a car
questions.explanation: „Der Strom“ is electricity as well as a large river or current, and „sparen“ is to save. A storm is „der Sturm“.

questions.stem: Read: „Roboter übernehmen in vielen Fabriken einfache Aufgaben. Dadurch fallen manche Arbeitsplätze weg, gleichzeitig entstehen neue Berufe in der IT.“ Which statement matches the text?
options: Factories are hiring more workers for simple tasks
Some jobs disappear while new IT jobs appear
Robots have replaced every factory job
IT jobs are disappearing because of robots
questions.explanation: „Fallen weg“ is 'disappear', and „manche“ limits it to some jobs. „Gleichzeitig entstehen“ is 'at the same time arise', so new IT jobs appear rather than vanish.

questions.stem: What is Carl Benz known for?
options: Building one of the first petrol-driven cars
Building the first electric train in the world
questions.explanation: Benz patented his three-wheeled motor car in 1886. The diesel engine is named after Rudolf Diesel, and the rigid airship after Ferdinand von Zeppelin.

questions.stem: The MP3 audio format was largely developed at which German research organisation?
questions.explanation: Researchers at a Fraunhofer institute in Erlangen led the work on MP3. The Max Planck Society does basic research, while the Goethe-Institut and Deutsche Welle promote German language and media abroad.
